city-digital-twin · Newcastle study · project report

The seventeenth project report - city-digital-twin

2026-11-07HEAD 079a49abranch praneetdhoolia/revive-after-host-resetgate PASSED on the branch (26 checks); on main at Phase 0: FAILED - doc currency, board blocks, issues gated (gh unauthenticated after the reset)

Built well, held back by its host, not its model. Two of twelve modes are inside 10 % on F39's control (car +8.5 %, motorbike -4.1 %), unchanged since the sixteenth report, because nothing has reached a reading since: the treatment arm that tests the pt frequency term was killed by three manual restarts, run warm to iteration 50, stopped by the operator for a shared host, and then lost every plans checkpoint when the host was reset - with all 81 aborted raw directories. Nothing in the harness copies a checkpoint out of results/raw, and that one gap now costs more than every result-preserving speed-up the performance pass found put together (about 1 h an arm). The code and controls are sound and the gate passes; 58 findings (6 defects, 18 risks, 34 smells) are mostly in the harness's handling of stopped arms and in instruments that say less than they appear to. In its field the twin is still the only project attempting per-mode ridership on every mode, ahead on physical fidelity and behind on calibration cost: the field now calibrates inside one run, where this project pays a ~28 h arm per evaluation. The 2026 evidence (Wardman et al.; England's NTS0702) supports the treatment's ATAP M1 form, and points the car-less' missing alternative at transit, not at lifts.

Method

Six lanes, one agent each (code, performance, history, documents and issues, field, factors), over the mechanical half from the five collectors at HEAD 079a49a3. The GitHub half was collected on 7 November after gh was re-authenticated. Phase 6 spent 32 of 40 calls over 6 rounds, Phase 7 35 of 40 over 9; both libraries written before return. Ten cited file:lines were re-read by the writer and five searched rows re-fetched; none was dropped. Ratings 1-5 per area on the rubric in the appendix, never averaged.

Narrative

10 Aug: one day built the data package, the network and the demand (PRs #1-#3); MATSim first loaded the inputs on 11 Aug (#4). 11-24 Aug: the registry, the issue-32 rebuild, ride pairing, freight and every person mode made physical; the first completed 25 % arms (F4, 21 Aug) gave C5. 25 Aug-7 Sep: family after family (F6-F30, eight on 30 Aug alone) stopped at iteration-100 gates; bus (1 Sep) and car (7 Sep) first read inside 10 % at a gate. 3 Sep: the first project report; the issue gate (#111) and a report every one to two days followed, mostly fixing instruments. 9 Sep: the first result since F4 (F32, 0 of 12); 12-14 Sep the footpath network (F34) and F35 arm 0, the first result with 2 of 12. 14-18 Sep: documents moved to docs/ and split from the city; the routers and scoring pairs both read null against arm 0. 19-22 Sep: Mumbai lands on the framework contract (#240-#251) and pauses on a host it cannot have (D15). 22-30 Sep: roots rebuild (F36), its arm killed by Windows Update at 237; F37 and F38 results; F39's control a result, 2 of 12, motorbike back in the band. 7-8 Oct: report #16, every no-run fix it named, D29-D32 answered, the TfNSW request sent after nine issuances, the headway treatment launched. 8-9 Oct: three Start-menu restarts and a co-tenant cost the treatment 15.3 h; the operator paused it at iteration 50. 9 Oct-6 Nov: nothing - no commit, run or session; the host reset took every aborted raw directory and the treatment's checkpoints. 6-7 Nov: the sixty-sixth session revives the toolchain and corrects the board (uncommitted); this report, at the user's request, follows no new result.

Three questions

is the code reproducible
Mostly, with two new holes. Builds: code_metrics finds 0 unseeded random draws in the build layers; globs and feeds are sorted (build_matsim_network.py:113-115); build_manifest no longer stamps a wall-clock generated (build_manifest.py:937); the 25 wall-clock reads in the build layers are retrieval stamps and timings. Holes: a truncated download can be recorded as an immutable raw file (fetch_with_provenance.py:56-61, 81), and build_timing books crashed builders as ok (build_timing.py:123). Runs: pt2matsim mapping and MATSim are not bit-reproducible by the project's own rule, so reproducibility of an arm rests on its plans checkpoints - which nothing protects (results_store.py:425, prune_run.py:43), and the one paused arm lost them all to the host reset (processed record reached_iteration 50, no raw directory).
is it city-agnostic
Largely, and better than at the sixteenth report: check_hardcoding and check_manifest run --all-cities in the gate and CI, check_city now refuses undeclared place names in city scripts (check_city.py:431), check_city_agnostic.py proves a re-identified city resolves. Remaining one-city structure in the framework: ROAD_VEHICLE_MODES omits Mumbai's declared auto_rickshaw (extract_metrics.py:85 vs cities/mumbai/city.json:50) with three more literal mode lists; build_data_dictionary.py's GROUPS are Newcastle's directories and schema letters, leaving 34 of Mumbai's 156 processed CSVs undocumented; a structural exemption in check_hardcoding.py:891 is justified by 'this city's observed means'. Newcastle itself carries 15 and Mumbai 159 recorded hardcoding items.
what would most cut its size
Removing narrative from code and repeated bootstraps, not deleting function: comment-only plus docstring lines are 20.0% of 99,783 Python lines in src/, tests/, the city adapters and run.py (27.6-35% in the largest modules: run_matsim.py 35%, build_matsim_run_inputs.py 33%, build_activity_chains.py 30%); the 168 three-line build_timing blocks (~500 lines) collapse into one bootstrap hook; check_hardcoding's 179 exemptions move to data (400-600 lines of Python); run_matsim.main (65 lines) and prune_run.py (143) can go; the Mumbai harbour scripts can share primitives (300-500 lines). Together roughly 3,000-5,000 lines of Python with every behaviour kept - a few per cent of the code; the bulk is real function.

architecture
Framework builders under src/build read city paths through src/city.py and declared values through the registry; city adapters under cities/<city>/build turn that city's raw tables into the framework's processed shapes. build_activity_chains -> build_matsim_plans -> build_matsim_run_inputs is the demand-to-config chain; build_manifest walks OUTPUT_INPUTS declarations into MANIFEST.csv lineage; build_timing records each builder's wall time through an atexit hook that 168 scripts now install in their __main__ block.

defectsrc/build/build_timing.py123start()'s atexit handler decides status from sys.exc_info(), which is (None, None, None) inside an atexit callback, so every builder that crashed or refused is recorded 'ok'. Probed this pass on Python 3.14: an uncaught ValueError leaves sys.exc_info()[0] None (sys.last_exc is the ValueError) and SystemExit('REFUSED') likewise.Measured: both committed _build_timing.json files carry only status ok (Newcastle 21, Mumbai 9) and performance.json reports failed: [] for Mumbai; a builder that dies after 40 minutes is booked as a 40-minute successful build in the reproduction-pipeline cost the performance pass prices.new

architecture
run.py is the operator's front door; it resolves the registry, runs the issue gate, preflight (every refusal except the subsample) and the arm-fraction refusal, then re-invokes itself under the Windows Task Scheduler (or a setsid session on POSIX) with --issue-gate-passed --foreground; the scheduled child proves its launch by stamp+nonce against the live task (scheduler_launched) and calls run_matsim.run(). run_matsim.run() reconciles stale cards, migrates the store, applies the launch refusals, matches a completed prior by identity hashes (controler/values/inputs sha256), writes the card, emits config.xml from the registry, starts the JVM with three daemon watchers (gate, ceiling, stall; the last two now share _start_bound_watch) and an async raw trim, and closes the run out at whichever boundary ended it. results_store owns where bytes live: records mirror into results/processed at every transition; results/raw is a budgeted cache trimmed oldest-first. --stop writes an operator marker, kills harness then JVM, decides died vs stopped from the log, closes out, extracts metrics, mirrors and trims; --pause (PR #267) adds resumable: true to the record so resolve_warm_start accepts it. A warm start copies the parent's newest output/ITERS/it.N/N.plans.xml.gz into the new run and re-derives the innovation fraction so the jar cutoff is the parent's.

defectsrc/run/results_store.py425Nothing protects a warm-start checkpoint. trim() (425-555) and reclaim() (558-611) delete a raw run whose findings are in processed without reading its record's resumable flag or a died completion; RECORD_FILES (38-45) mirrors no plans checkpoint; stop_run itself calls extract_metrics and trim right after writing resumable: true (run_matsim.py:2493, 2506-2512), which makes the paused run an ordinary trim candidate (it now has _run.json and _metrics.json). There is no copy of the newest N.plans.xml.gz anywhere but results/raw on the one disk.Measured this pass: results/processed/aborted_20261008T212704_250it_25pct/_run.json carries completion stopped_by_operator, reached_iteration 50, resumable true, wall_s 26521.4, and results/raw holds no directory for it (processed/_trim_log.json has no entry for it, so the store did not delete it - the host reset did). Every plans checkpoint went with raw, so --warm-start cannot resume it and its 7.4 h are lost. The same loss follows without a reset: the next launch's _trim_async (run_matsim.py:2845) over a raw cache above RUN.storage.raw_cap_gb = 500 deletes a paused or died arm oldest-first once its extract grace (3600 s) has passed.new
defectsrc/run/prune_run.py43prune_run deletes output/ITERS (PRUNABLE, 43) from any run with _run.json and _metrics.json whose card is not running (61-78), on the premise in its docstring (4-15) that 'nothing in src/analyse or src/calibrate reads that directory' and that 'a run is seeded and deterministic, so re-running reproduces it'. Both are false today: 22 references to ITERS in 10 src/analyse modules (iteration_reading.iterations_with reads output/ITERS/it.N tables; the board's scoreboard and trend read them) and resolve_warm_start reads output/ITERS/it.N/N.plans.xml.gz; CLAUDE.md states MATSim runs are not bit-reproducible. It composes results/ itself (RESULTS, 39) although results_store says deleting from raw is that module's call and nobody else's. README.md:125 advertises it.python src/run/prune_run.py --all after a pause deletes the ITERS of the paused arm (status aborted, _run.json and _metrics.json present): its plans checkpoints, its per-iteration trips tables and therefore every reading the board and report_mode_ridership --trend take from it, and stamps _pruned.json saying 're-running reproduces what was removed'.new

architecture
Readers take a run through results_store.resolve_or_die; iteration_reading owns table paths, the run record and (since PR #262) the one citable-iteration clamp; report_mode_ridership turns a trips/legs table into the twelve-mode table against targets and is also the gate watcher's subprocess; summarise_run now makes ONE events pass at close-out whose sidecar the station tally and transit traversals reuse; build_status_board generates the board's blocks; arm_cost prices an arm from the newest probe's own stopwatch and host history; fit/calibrate score the calibration split.

architecture
The registry schema rejects an undeclared value; check_hardcoding asks five questions (unwired, report-only, template literals, script decisions, coordinates) plus wall clock, and is at 0 OUTSIDE each city's recorded debt; debt_ledger is the one shape for hardcoding and manifest debt (ceiling equals the item count; a rise against origin/main needs a new ceiling_log entry with raised: true). check_manifest judges raw retrieval dates, lineage scope, processed source, byte drift and declared producers per city. session_gate runs everything --all-cities; CI runs the same in test.yml and the Java probes in java-probes.yml.

architecture
Extractors fetch into data/raw with a provenance record (URL, retrieval date, licence) and transform into data/processed; build_manifest hashes every artefact and resolves lineage, licence and share-alike ancestry; check_manifest judges the rows against rules with each city's recorded debt. Newcastle's three fetchers now share fetch_with_provenance.fetch_all and its two RMS extractors share rms_hourly.

MATSim extensions
inventory
  • src/java/citysim/*.java (69 files) - CitysimControler (entry point, module groups), RidePairingEngine (1,721), TaxiFleetEngine, HiredFleetQueue, ServiceQualityScoring, PtUnservedScoring, EscortCoherenceListener, HouseholdVehicleRoster, HouseholdCarDepartureHandler, GenericRouteTeleporter, NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter, ActivityLinkCapacity, ActivityLinkAssigner, AvailabilityModesCalculator, GatedSubtourModeChoice, RemodeRestore, RunTelemetry, fare and parking handlers; 13 *Probe/*Scan classes
  • src/java_signals/citysim/*.java - CitysimSignalsControler, ScatsSignalController, TramPriorityController and their probes
  • tests/fixtures/*Probe.java - probe fixtures
architecture
CitysimControler binds MATSim extension points: permissible modes, ride pairing re-timed in beforeMobsim, a finite taxi/hired fleet with refused-trip re-moding and restore, household vehicle rosters, service-quality and unserved-pt scoring via PersonScoreEvent, generic route teleport restricted to declared stub modes, telemetry requiring the sim-step barrier. The signals stack is a separate Maven-built classpath. Since the sixteenth report each citysim listener logs listener=<name> ms=<n> per iteration, ServiceQualityScoring resolves departures per vehicle arrival instead of per boarding and stamps its charge at qsim end time, ScatsSignalController refuses to start without the barrier, and TaxiFleetProbe (251 lines) and EscortCoherenceProbe (+80) were added.

mobsim

threads_vs_cores
qsim numberOfThreads 16 (RUN.machine.threads, run identity), replanning (global) 20, events handler threads 4 on 24 logical cores (gc.log 'CPUs: 24 total'); ParallelGC 18 workers
qsim_settings
PassingQ, trafficDynamics queue, flow and storage capacity 0.25, stuckTime 10 s, removeStuckVehicles false, endTime 30:00:00, main modes car/truck/motorbike/walk/bike/taxi, synchronizeOnSimSteps true, oneThreadPerHandler false (config.xml:38-48, 359-361)
load_per_iteration
2,952,577 departures (median, telemetry.jsonl); at it.99 2,943,827, of which network walk 1,156,105 and non-network walk 1,236,982 (81 % walks), car 386,357, ride 88,498, bike 25,589, truck 24,004; 2,139 transit vehicles in 4 types (transitVehicles.xml.gz); stuck median 5,745 (3,243-25,253), 0.19 % of departures
pace
8,451 departures per wall second (median, performance.json telemetry); mobsim median 239 s (control), 205-249 s on probes; event-writing iterations pay +80-170 s inside the mobsim (it.100 318 s, it.250 408 s)
thread_scaling
measured once, on F27 (§9.147): mobsim 139-143 s at 10 threads, 134-137 at 16, 131-132 at 24 - 2.4x the threads bought 8 %; never re-measured on the F34+ footpath network
fraction_scaling
1 % -> 25 %: mobsim 28-44 s -> 205-249 s (~6-7x for 25x agents). The sampling position page states no pace-vs-fraction law to test against (docs/positions/sampling-and-families.md), so 'scales as the page says' is unanswerable; RUN.monitor.pace_band_s [217, 253] is the old 25 % x 1000 band and every F35+ arm sits above it
gpu
Nothing in the stack can use a GPU: the 510 jars under .tools carry no CUDA/OpenCL/JOCL/Aparapi/TornadoVM library, requirements.txt pins no torch/cupy/numba/jax, src/ and config/ name no GPU, and MATSim's QSim runs its 16 QSimEngine threads on the JVM (config.xml:42, gc.log 'CPUs: 24'). The RTX 5090's Code 43 costs the simulator nothing. Its one indirect effect is on co-tenancy: the operator's GPU applications (Blender was the probe's co-tenant at 1.0-2.14 cores) now run on the CPU the arm shares

strategies
ChangeExpBeta 0.7, ReRoute 0.15, SubtourModeChoice 0.1 (gated, persons only), TimeAllocationMutator 0.05 (RUN.replanning.weights); innovation off after 0.8 x 250 = it.200; plan memory 8; WorstPlanSelector; 20 threads
router_calls_it100

19,424 s = 5.40 h per arm (19.7 %); innovating median 78 s (max 972 s under the co-tenant band), tail median 2 s; the tail iteration is 284 s against 346 s innovating

plans 12 x 1,011.6 MB = 12.14 GB at it.0,1,25,...,250 (dump all plans 2,548 s = 0.71 h = 2.6 % of the iteration sum, 2.84 % by performance.json); events 4 x 1,559 MB = 6.24 GB at it.0,100,200,250 (+80-170 s inside each mobsim); experienced plans 11 x 299 MB = 3.29 GB (iterationEnds 38-349 s on those iterations, ~1,050 s per arm above the 2 s plain median, shared with the trips/linkstats writes); legs/trips/activities 27 each = 2.18 GB; linkstats 5 x 30 MB; signalEvents2Via 4 x 36 MB; ITERS 24.24 GB + output/ 3.08 GB = ~26-27 GB per 25 % arm
store
results/raw 353 GiB in 96 dirs against RUN.storage.raw_cap_gb 500 - room for ~5 more arms before trim; bytes on disk across all runs 377.3 GB (performance.json)
observers
progress_digest every RUN.monitor.progress_interval_s = 30 s: reads matsim.log INCREMENTALLY from a saved offset (run_view.read_iterations, #131), modestats, one psutil host sample appended to _host.jsonl (123 lines for the 1.06 h probe), one atomic _progress.json; the gate/ceiling/stall watchers share the same offset cache - negligible against a 345 s iteration. Defect of placement: _host.jsonl and gc.log live only in results/raw and are not mirrored to processed (results/processed/aborted_20261008T212704_250it_25pct has neither), so the treatment's host history died with its raw dir

jvm

given
-Xms=-Xmx (run_matsim.py:2806), -XX:+UseParallelGC (RUN.machine.gc_collector), -Xlog:gc* (RUN.machine.gc_log true), JFR off (RUN.machine.jfr_profile false); JDK 25.0.4+7; 48g on the control, 38g on the treatment and its probe (f39_headway_25pct.json); gc.log init: 'Compressed Oops: Disabled', 'Large Page Support: Disabled', Parallel Workers 18
rule
RUN.machine.heap_floor_gib 15.6 + heap_per_fraction_gib 87 x 0.25 = 37.35 GiB (refuse_small_heap, run_matsim.py:1012); refuse_unsafe_host (run_matsim.py:912) needs free RAM >= xmx + RUN.machine.free_ram_margin_gib 6
peak_vs_live
control: peak used 45,149 MB of 47,104 (ParallelGC fills the heap); live after 356 Allocation-Failure full collections 19,059-30,063 MB, last 21,450 MB; probe at 38g: live 13,830-22,639 MB
gc
control 8,612 s of pauses = 8.59 % of wall (full 6,086 s / 356, young 2,526 s / 7,580; 123 full pauses over 10 s sum 5,264 s, max 537 s); F37 arm 13,215 s = 11.68 % (max full 915.7 s); probe at 38g 49 s = 1.29 % over 1.06 h. A 537-916 s full collection of a ~40 GB heap is paging, not collecting. docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:36 still says 'GC under 1 % of wall' (§9.169, F35 arm 0) - stale against both F37 and F39
binding
the heap was never the OOM constraint; the HOST's RAM was: 48 GB fixed + JVM overhead on 63.5 GiB leaves ~13 GB for everything else, and the treatment ran at 0.2-4.8 GiB free with an 8,249 s iteration. Both heaps sit above the ~32 GB compressed-oops ceiling, so every reference costs 8 bytes; whether a <=31g heap with compressed oops holds the live set (30.1 GB measured uncompressed) is unmeasured - needs a probe arm, and the heap rule was measured uncompressed
new_host
after the reset the host is the same Core Ultra 9 275HX / 24 threads / 63.5 GiB with 44 GiB free at idle: 48g + 6 = 54 GiB is refused; 38g + 6 = 44 GiB passes only at exactly idle, so any co-tenant re-opens the refusal (the 8 October launch overrode the margin to 2)

python

post_run
control: _run.json 11:14:13 -> _metrics.json 11:38:18 (~24 min, from file mtimes); _fit.json later (16:17) by hand. The close-out now decodes the 1.6 GB output_events.xml.gz ONCE (summarise_run.events_pass, summarise_run.py:260-308) for the accounting, report_mode_ridership's count-station tally and transit_link_delays' traversals, recorded in output/_events_pass_it250.json (5.1 MB) and consumed via recorded_events_pass; frontage_volumes.py and replay_events.py still read the events on their own, but they are on-demand instruments, not the close-out
finding
no stage of the post-run chain records its own wall time (no elapsed field in _summary.json, _metrics.json or _run.json; summarise_run.py and extract_metrics.py call no timer) - the 24 min is inferred from mtimes. Write it beside the stage's output (e.g. _metrics.json 'extract_s', _summary.json 'events_pass_s')
during_run
progress_digest and the watchers read the log incrementally (#131) and one host sample per 30 s - no measurable cost

build

finding
the skill's premise that no producer records its wall time is now partly out of date: cities/newcastle/data/_build_timing.json times 21 builders, 6,843.9 s (1.90 h): build_activity_chains.py 5,058 s (73.9 %, 27 Sep), build_matsim_run_inputs.py 1,169 s, build_matsim_network.py 249 s, build_matsim_plans.py 176 s, build_matsim_signals.py 78 s; 29 manifest producers are untimed (every extract_*/fetch_*, calibrate.py, build_params.py, measure_* among them). Mumbai: 9 timed, 414 s; 95 untimed (performance.json build_timing)
recommend
stamp the 29 untimed Newcastle producers through the same build_timing helper (the 15 instrumented-but-unrecorded of the last report are now partly recorded: 18 -> 21) and profile build_activity_chains.py, the build's critical path; 0 arm hours, quotes the rebuild from a record

warm start

mechanism
resolve_warm_start (run_matsim.py:193-285) takes the newest output/ITERS/it.N/N.plans.xml.gz of a died (or paused, fde7b27e) run plus its _meta.json/_config.json, copies it into the new run dir (run_matsim.py:346-357) and re-derives the innovation cutoff; a resume sets up in 3.6-3.8 min (routed plans, §9.215) and its first iteration re-reads the 1 GB checkpoint (~600 s against ~350)
checkpoint_cadence
write_plans_interval 25 on arms: 12 dumps, 0.71 h and 12.14 GB per arm; a death costs at most 24 iterations (~2.3 h at 345 s). Moving to 50 would save 5 dumps (~0.29 h, ~5 GB) and double the worst-case loss to ~4.7 h - on this host's record (6 deaths in two families) 25 stands
survives_host_loss
a restart or crash: YES - F38 resumed from 75, 175 and 225 and finished as a result; F39's treatment resumed from 25. A host RESET/reimage: NO - checkpoints live only in results/raw/<run>/output/ITERS on the one disk. After the November reset results/raw holds 96 dirs (353 GiB), none named aborted_; 81 aborted_ dirs present in processed/ have no raw dir and no _trim_log.json entry (the trim log ends 8 September), among them every F38/F39 attempt, so the treatment's it.25 and it.50 checkpoints are gone and the arm restarts from 0
copy_cost
one checkpoint = N.plans.xml.gz 1.02-1.20 GB (control: it.25 1,195,374,768 B, it.250 1,017,577,930 B, mean 1,011.6 MB over 12) + _meta.json 1.6 KB + _config.json 431 KB + _run.json 1.5 KB + config.xml 21 KB = ~1.0-1.2 GB; newest-only retention ~1.2 GB standing, every checkpoint of an arm (it.25-250) ~10.4 GB. Copy wall time to a second disk or an off-host store: unmeasured - needs a probe arm (copy after it.N+1 begins, never while the dump is written)
on_this_report
no warm start is possible for the treatment; the control needs none

Verdict on the 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon is reachable at the measured pace: F39's control did it in 27.85 h in one JVM (345 s median, 346 s innovating, 284 s after the cutoff), and on an untouched host its own stopwatch prices the same arm at ~25.8 h. What has stopped the project since is not pace but the host: of the 79.8 machine hours the F38 and F39 arms spent, ~17.5 h (22 %) were destroyed by host events - a storage-driver bugcheck, four operator restarts or shutdowns, a co-tenant that pushed free RAM to 0.2 GiB and one iteration to 8,249 s, and a reset that took every aborted_ raw dir and with it the treatment's checkpoints - so the treatment restarts from iteration 0 needing 27.9 h against the 24.2 h left on D29. Halving an arm (~14 h) is not reachable by any measured result-preserving lever: the taxi walk cache (0.6-0.79 h), experienced plans at the final only (0.15-0.29 h) and the early dumps (0.06 h) sum to about 1 h, build-time routing (0.33 h) possibly touches results, and a cloud or D15 host buys at most 3 % from cores (16 -> 24 threads, §9.147) - its value is solitude, worth 2-12 h only against a shared run. What could halve it is inside the 18.2 h mobsim (66 %), where 81 % of the 2.95 M departures are walks: whether its time goes to the qsim's walk legs, our telemetry and signal handlers, or thread imbalance is unmeasured - needs a probe arm (the JFR probe, #231), and a 31g compressed-oops heap against GC at 8.6-11.7 % of wall is likewise unmeasured. Before any of that, the cheapest hours are operational: keep the arm alone, and copy each 1.0-1.2 GB checkpoint off results/raw so a host loss costs 24 iterations rather than the arm.

what the comparison says

  • The top rung (every simulated mode scored against a band) is still empty across 63 rows; this project is the only attempt and reads 2 of 12 inside 10 % on F39's control (car +8.5 %, motorbike -4.1 %).
  • The field converged this autumn on what this project enforces: shares are necessary but not sufficient (Paris, Tel Aviv, MWCOG all say it in print), and missing demand is derived from counts rather than absorbed in a constant (Paris background traffic).
  • Agency activity-based models routinely miss transit first time by about 20 % (MWCOG) and fix it by alternating calibration and validation; the residual misses sit on small or peculiar services - SEMCOG -79 % and -95 % on two small operators, PSRC ferry -82 % (stored) - the same family as this project's light rail -74 % and ferry +95 %.
  • Where the field is moving fastest is calibration cost: in-run online calibration in ~60 iterations (Dib & Balac), raptor calibration with no mobsim (eqasim CH), seven of 28 count sites from purchased travel times (Meerut). This project pays a ~28 h 25 % arm per evaluation and its contraction test is held.
  • Calibrated MATSim city models state their bill when they state it at all: Winnipeg 27 full runs for five modes; Rotterdam, Cape Town and others by hand (stored). None reaches twelve modes.
  • Physical fidelity is this project's clearest lead: the new rows teleport walk and bike, run buses at steady speed or scale car time by an hourly factor; none runs every pt access walk as a network leg.
  • Generative LLM agents are not yet a better route to an observed split: on Toulouse's 2023 survey the fitted choice models beat the best tuned LLM (3.43-4.38 vs 4.86 composite).
  • Acceptance bands are becoming contractual (Tel Aviv: PT share +/-3 pp, >=90 % of line-directions within +/-15 %), which gives this project's self-imposed 10 % / 20 % gates their first published analogue in a client contract.

what each does best that we lack

fromlacksource
eqasim Switzerland (Dib & Balac, arXiv 2610.32698)Calibration inside one run: constants updated from logged replanning mini-batches, converging in ~60 iterations at 2-3 min per iteration - no arm per evaluation.https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32698v1
MWCOG Gen3 v1.1.0An explicit calibration-validation alternation (survey shares <-> boarding counts) with sub-mode E/O published after each round.https://www.mwcog.org/assets/1/6/Gen3_Model_v1.1.0_Calibration_Efforts_v4.pdf
Tel Aviv (Replan / Netivei Ayalon)Acceptance criteria fixed before the run and a transferability test with the count correction removed; the mechanism written beside every outlier.https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2026/presentations/107-17-volotskiy.pdf
Paris (Samaei et al.)Travel-time perception error estimated against TomTom route times by OD class, period and distance band, and background demand solved from count residuals.https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2026/presentations/107-02-samaei.pdf
Meerut (Ashutosh et al.)Observation priced and targeted: rank intersections on purchased travel-time data, count only the queue-dominated ones; a calibration loop that rolls back and halves its step on deterioration.https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2026/presentations/107-03-ashutosh.pdf
Winnipeg (Predhumeau & Manley)The calibrated split replicated on two further independent samples - a measured replication band (this project's D30 seeds lane, unrun).https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.11416
SEMCOG ActSim v1.3The new model validated side by side with its predecessor on the same counts and screenlines, and boardings by operator with a stated reason for each miss.https://semcog.github.io/TDM_ActSim/SEMCOG_ABM_Calibration_And_Validation.pdf
Toulouse generative agents (Bru et al.)Code, seeds and the evaluation population released together so a fit can be re-scored by a third party.https://github.com/Ytlse/generative-agents-urban-mobility

ours

name
city-digital-twin - Newcastle (NSW) study (this repository)
engine
MATSim end to end, with project-owned Java extensions (src/java/citysim, src/java_signals) for signals, ride pairing and mode-specific constraints
city_population
Newcastle (NSW) region - five LGAs, 1,500 core SA1s, base year 2026
sample_fraction
25 % (standing directive since 1 Sep 2026). The NEWEST RESULT is F39's CONTROL 20260929T072135_250it_25pct (_run.json): fraction 0.25, iterations 250, reached_iteration 250, completion ran_to_last_iteration, rc 0, 16 threads, xmx 48g, seed 20260810, NO warm start, wall_s 100,268.6 (27.85 h; the board says 27.9 h against a 27.7 h quote), median_iteration_s 345.28; persons_in 622,174, persons_kept 158,161 (unit household; 111,828 without a household). Transit capacities scaled to the fraction (seats 44 -> 11, 60 -> 15, 98 -> 24.5; pce 2.8 -> 0.7).
modes
TWELVE, each scored individually: car, ride, walk, taxi, bike, motorbike, bus, heavy_rail, light_rail, ferry, truck, freight_train - every one represented in the mobsim; motorbike now CHOSEN by daily use from one household motorcycle (B.motorbike.representation = choice, daily_use_ratio 0.1801 from ABS SMVU NSW; section 9.218)
active_modes
physical, on the footpath network of 12 September (40,203 harvested path ways as walk/bike links; walk permitted on 363,818 links, bike on 265,523; pedestrians at 1.25 m/s, cyclists at 4.2 m/s, path links uncongested). pt access, egress and transfer walks are NETWORK LEGS the qsim executes (RUN.routing.access_egress_type = accessEgressModeToLink; RUN.transit_router.access_egress_basis = network; teleported = 0 on a full arm, sections 9.167 and 9.219); a no-route walk beyond 3,224 m is an unexecutable plan (section 9.219: 358,146 refused; 47.6 % of 2,000,000 pt requests had no transit route). F39's control: walk 10.0835 vs 13.4 % (-24.7 %) at 3.75 km mean against 0.70; bike 5.5021 vs 2.2084 % (+149.1 %) at 7.54 km against 5.2 with a distance cost of -0.000192308 utils/m (positions/walk-and-bike.md).
pt_physical
yes - bus, heavy rail, light rail and ferry run the mapped GTFS schedule on the mapped network (15 feeds, 0 unmapped stops); access/egress/transfer walks routed on the footpath network; a headway charge on the boarded LINE at its stop (citysim.ServiceQualityScoring behind C.time_weights.service_quality_representation, with C.time_weights.service_interval_function = linear | atap_m1) is BUILT and UNRUN - the F39 treatment waits on D29 (section 9.219)
signals
yes - SCATS implemented as its published algorithm (6 A.signals.scats.* fields: target degree of saturation, cycle step, min/max cycle, DS deadband and smoothing) on 14 explicit corridor signal systems (54 signalised approaches), transit signal priority (7 A.signals.tsp.* fields: green extension, 12 s window, 120 m detection, 0.2 budget share, compensation) and 14 A.crossings.* fields for timetable-derived level-crossing closures. The offset library is swept because it is unpublished. Counted from cities/newcastle/registry/*.json at HEAD 1b14e559.
freight
yes - truck as a road vehicle from 6 B.freight.* fields (trip ratio, gravity beta, PCE, speed, length), scored on network-wide road-vehicle share as a level only (5.4694 % against 15.4698 % at the count stations; the target basis is the stations, --truck-stations); freight rail as timetable-derived level-crossing closures (405 movements a weekday: 313 scheduled plus 44 and 48 freight at the two crossings, 277 s each) rather than a mobsim vehicle
fares_pricing
yes - Opal fare schedule in the registry (38 A.fare.* fields: peak/off-peak by mode, concession, caps, distance bands), priced parking with search time (14 A.parking.* fields), income-scaled marginal utility of money (C.income.representation, exponent 1.0 sweep 0.5-1.5, top band x1.25), a monetary distance rate (C.scoring.monetary_distance_rate) and a motorbike fuel ratio 0.5351 of the car rate (ABS SMVU). Counted at HEAD 1b14e559.
validation_rung
per-mode ridership, every simulated mode - the top rung, and still the only project in this survey of 55 attempting it for twelve modes. The pass of 9 September qualified the claim (a four-step model, WFTDM, does report six transit modes inside 10%); THIS pass qualifies it further and more precisely: the WFRC ActivitySim framework's own Table 29 lists 'Transit boardings by transit mode' as a standard validation summary, so per-transit-mode granularity is normal agency practice for an activity-based model. What no other row does is treat every one of twelve modes as a SCORED TARGET WITH A BAND that the calibration is obliged to satisfy simultaneously. | 2026-09-16: unchanged - still the only row in 55 that scores every simulated mode as a target with a band; BEAM CORE, read this pass, names three observation families (speeds/VMT, MTC shares, agency boardings) and publishes no level fit for any. | 2026-09-29 (fifteenth pass): unchanged - still the only row in 58 scoring every simulated mode as a target with a band; the reading on it fell from 2 to 1 of 12 inside 10 % (F38's arm 0). The field's nearest agency analogues (PSRC per operator, MWCOG and CMAP per transit mode) validate transit by operator or submode, not every mode at once. | 2026-10-07 (sixteenth pass): unchanged in kind - still the only row in 61 scoring every simulated mode as a target with a band; the reading is back to 2 of 12 inside 10 % on F39's control. The field now holds TWO agency rows with per-transit-type deviation tables (MWCOG 2025; PSRC 2015, read this pass, which names a ferry miss of -81.9 % AM and a light-rail miss of -39.9 % midday - the two families this project misses most), and a NEW ROW (Jakarta MRT) on the transit-ridership rung for a single mode. | 2026-11-06 (seventeenth pass): unchanged in kind against 63 rows - still the only row scoring every simulated mode as a target with a band. Nearest this pass: Winnipeg (five modes each inside a stated band, on survey shares only), Tel Aviv (contractual PT-share and line-direction bands), MWCOG v1.1.0 (transit sub-mode E/O 0.97-1.01) and SEMCOG (boardings by operator, two small operators -79 % and -95 %).
best_fit
IN CALIBRATION, 2 OF 12 MODES INSIDE 10 % AT THE NEWEST RESULT. The board's scoreboard block at HEAD 1b14e559 (F39's control 20260929T072135_250it_25pct, family F39-motorcycles-by-daily-use-trip-ends-on-carrying-links-and-a-bounded-walk, 25 %, 250 of 250, ran_to_last_iteration; reproduce with python src/analyse/report_mode_ridership.py --run 20260929T072135_250it_25pct --it 250), trips table: car +8.5 % (63.2999 vs 58.3222 % share), ride -25.0 % (15.4418 vs 20.6000), walk -24.7 % (10.0835 vs 13.4000), taxi +161.1 % (2.5892 vs 0.9916), bike +149.1 % (5.5021 vs 2.2084), motorbike -4.1 % (0.3629 vs 0.3785), bus -30.7 % (1.6498 vs 2.3819), heavy_rail +119.3 % (14,320 vs 6,529 boardings per weekday, x1/fraction), light_rail -74.0 % (768 vs 2,954), ferry +95.4 % (1,544 vs 790.2850); truck level-only (5.4694 vs 15.4698 % network-wide road-vehicle share, not the target basis), freight_train representation-only (405 vs 405). Inside 10 %: car, motorbike. Past the 20 % stop bar: ride, walk, taxi, bike, bus, heavy_rail, light_rail, ferry (eight). F38's result (1 of 12) is a direction only; nothing compares across the family boundary (section 3.5).
open_source
yes - the repository; OSM-derived layers ODbL 1.0, the rest CC-BY 4.0
reproducible
yes and gated - every derived file regenerable by a committed script from immutable hashed raw downloads; 968 files in data/MANIFEST.csv (733 CC-BY 4.0 / 220 ODbL 1.0 / 15 bespoke) with hash, rows, producing script, source, licence and retrieval date; everything synthetic seeded (20260810). A MATSim run is not bit-reproducible; comparisons are read as bands within one family.
city_agnostic
yes by construction and exercised - src/, config/schema/, tests/ and run.py read identically for an unseen city; all 604 registry fields (A 208, B 143, C 66, CAL 30, D 10, E 26, RUN 121), adapters and geometry live under cities/<city>/, enforced by check_city_agnostic.py and check_hardcoding.py --strict at 0. A second city (Mumbai) is built on the framework and is the delivery priority since 19 September 2026 (GOAL.md): 1 % cases ran; a 10 % probe waits on the D15 host.
status
active, in calibration - P4 at HEAD 079a49a3 (board last updated 6 November 2026, sixty-sixth session). Registry 604 fields, manifest 968 files, 30 assembled run-input sets (board state block). The newest RESULT is still F39's control (2 of 12 inside 10 %); F39's treatment arm (the headway charge, ATAP M1, D29) was STOPPED BY THE OPERATOR at iteration 50 on 9 October 2026 for the shared host, its plans checkpoints were lost in the host reset, and it relaunches from iteration 0 on a new approval (24.2 h of D29's 40 h left). Mumbai waits on the D15 host (384-512 GB).
does_best
Every controllable value declared with units, provenance and a sweep or held-fixed rule (558 fields), every living number pinned to its artefact by a check, twelve modes each monitored on its own basis every tenth iteration - and, unique in this survey, a REGISTRY-ENFORCED refusal to fit a constant over a named missing mechanism (C.asc.rail's departure_requires clause). THIS PASS ADDS A SECOND UNIQUENESS, AND IT IS THE HONEST ONE: the project's _fit.json scores mode shares, absolute link counts, trip-length geometry and vehicle occupancy IN ONE ARTEFACT FROM ONE RUN, names its 32 unscorable targets with reasons, and refuses to call a stopped arm a result. Across 53 surveyed projects, the closest published analogues each hold part of that - AToM validates five observation families but calibrates against one; Tallinn optimises three target families at once but reports no per-mode transit rung; the WFRC framework enumerates every validation summary but states outright that not all of them can be met simultaneously. | 2026-09-14: against the three rows added this pass the position sharpens - Cape Town reaches the tap-data rung for ONE operator with ~25 hand-tuned runs; mobiTopp Stuttgart calibrates trip-length distributions and modal split jointly but by eye; Barcelona runs generic actuated signals at 2,035 intersections on full demand for R2 0.81 on counts and nothing else. None scores more than one observation family with a stated band. | 2026-09-14 (tenth pass): the claim is now made against a RESULT with 2 of 12 inside 10 % rather than 0 - and against 55 rows. The two rows added this pass sharpen it from opposite sides: Barcelona-MATSim (2019) validates on counts it never calibrated on and names the excluded demand behind its two misses, which this project's fit module does for its 32 unscorable targets but not yet for its count outliers; Rotterdam-The Hague (2025) removes mode choice from MATSim altogether so that one calibrator owns it, where this project's twelve constants are scored inside the co-evolutionary loop they must survive. | 2026-09-16 (twelfth pass): the claim is now made against a THIRD result and the first one-field pair reading in the survey - a null. The BEAM update this pass sharpens the comparison from the sample side: BEAM calibrates at 10 %, validates at 30 % and states that an on-demand mode needs 40 % before its dynamics settle; this project reads taxi and ride at 25 % and scores them with a band, which no BEAM paper does. | 2026-09-29 (fifteenth pass): unchanged against 58 rows. The MUM 2026 programme shows the MATSim community moving toward automated multi-source calibration (seven talks), where this project's contraction test and _fit.json already sit; none of those talks yet publishes a per-mode band. | 2026-10-07 (sixteenth pass): against 61 rows. Three things read this pass bracket this project from new sides: Samaei et al. (Paris) publish exactly this project's count deficit and fix it with non-resident background demand rather than a constant - the same refusal this project's registry encodes for C.asc.rail; Dib & Balac fold the share calibration INTO the run at 8-13 % overhead, where this project pays one 28 h arm per evaluation; and PSRC's 2015 table shows an agency ABM missing ferry by -82 % and light rail by -40 % at midday while its total boardings sit within 2 % - the same two modes this project misses most, which says the miss is a known family, not a peculiarity of this twin. | 2026-11-06 (seventeenth pass): against 63 rows. The pass's new readings bracket it again: MWCOG states that a share-calibrated model first missed transit boardings by ~20 % and that reconciling the two has 'no standard procedure' - the reconciliation this project's _fit.json forces in one artefact; Winnipeg needed 27 full runs for five modes and checks the split on two more samples, the replication band this project has designed (D30) and not yet measured; Dib & Balac now publish the in-run calibration in full (about 60 iterations, 5 %), still the field's answer to the per-evaluation cost this project pays.

calibration_method
family
coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (unchanged, never run to completion) PLUS, NEW AT THIS HEAD AND NEVER RUN, an implemented ASC log-ratio fixed point - src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py. Read from the source at HEAD 781cf41, not searched.
what_the_source_says
src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 runs coordinate descent: per round, per free parameter, per grid point across that parameter's registry sweep, a FULL MATSim run -> extract_metrics -> fit -> a weighted scalar objective over declared _fit.json components, keeping a point only if it is feasible against the C4 occupancy and trip-length constraints; the round stops when the improvement falls below delta. The search space is DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY, not listed in the script: a field is free only if it is source=assumed, carries a scalar sweep and is not held_fixed. The six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore unreachable from the loop by construction - so this project has NO log(target/modelled) ASC loop of any kind. The one constant that is solved, asc_car_passenger, is solved in a separate module (solve_asc_ride.py:101-121) by SECANT INTERPOLATION ON log(ride_per_car) against the observed passenger:driver ratio, and is reported as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The loop refuses to fit more parameters than the objective identifies (four independent numbers) and cannot read a holdout row by construction.
objective_evaluations
coordinate descent: calibrate.py:433 computes the budget as sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs; at 25% an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall, so a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round search is ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours. THE LOOP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN TO COMPLETION. The ASC fixed point is far cheaper by design - TWO arms settle the contraction question - and is the only one of the two that has an evaluation count small enough to state in advance. Neither has been executed.
convergence_criterion
round-over-round objective improvement < delta

asc_fixed_point_new_this_pass
src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py EXISTS and PROPOSES ONLY; it has NEVER BEEN RUN. It applies delta_i = damping * [ ln(target_i/modelled_i) - ln(target_ref/modelled_ref) ] against car as reference - the same object as the Berry (1994) share inversion and the same expression matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes verbatim, with the damping declared on CAL.asc.damping. THREE DESIGN CHOICES ARE UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE TEST IS THE CONTRACTION, NOT THE SHARES - two damped rounds are compared mode by mode, and if |delta| shrinks the residual is a taste that constants will close, while if it does not shrink the deficit is STRUCTURAL and no constant will ever close it. That is a cheap, decisive, published-in-spirit answer to the 'constant or mechanism' question that the agency protocol answers only by ordering. (2) It CANNOT REACH A FROZEN CONSTANT: it reads held_fixed from the registry and refuses, structurally, the way the holdout guard refuses. (3) On heavy rail and light rail the step is marked basis_is_boardings and reported as a PROXY, because the logit inversion is exact only for shares of a common total. ROUND 1 IS PROPOSED OFF THE F31 GATE AND NOT APPLIED: bike -0.5121, bus -0.2301, ferry +0.6713, light rail +0.4143.
read_against_the_field_this_pass
Two published methods now bracket this project's loop and both were read this pass. (1) Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva (2020, TR-C 119:102650) names this project's coordinate descent for what it is: 'myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters' - and their non-myopic alternative calibrates precisely this project's target set at once (activity shares, mode shares, mode-specific OD flows, mode-specific sensor counts). (2) The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim framework publishes New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion) verbatim - the exact expression in asc_fixed_point.py - inside a CYCLIC protocol over model components, and states plainly that 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously.' | 2026-09-11 (third bracket): POLARIS's published procedure is the same cyclic ASC-by-purpose update, TIERED by iteration so that 'network state' can 'adapt to this change in demand' before the next tier is touched, with counts and speeds explicitly outside the calibrated set ('can only be minimally calibrated'). MATSim-NYC calibrated NO demand constants at all - its nested logit was estimated on RHTS + TLC/FHV/Citi Bike records and converted analytically - and spent its six SPSA iterations on twelve link-CAPACITY factors instead, which is the opposite allocation to this project's.

current_practice_2026
  • Wardman et al. 2026 (TR-A 207, March 2026): the walk/wait 2.0 convention is no longer supported (1.75 RP / 1.50 SP); headway guidance supported; congestion premium 1.33-1.51; reliability ratio 0.6-0.9; ATAP official values read through its Table 1. The registry sits at the top of the band on walk/wait and above it on reliability.
  • DfT NTS 2025 (September 2026): exact car-less mode splits; the paper-to-digital diary switch lowered recorded short walks - a series-break lesson for HTS targets.
  • MATSim 2026.0 (10 April 2026): core taste-variation options; Rakow & Nagel (MUM 2025) mixed-logit heterogeneity in MATSim is the practice frontier this model has only for income.
  • LLM-driven agents (GTA, CHI 2026): modal split within a few points of the survey but short trips under-produced by more than half; no LLM-MATSim coupling published.
  • No 2026 ATAP M1 revision found (the site timed out; the August 2021 technical report remains the newest found); no 2025/26 NSW HTS release found; no 2026 IPART point-to-point survey release found.
  • Context, not a factor: Hunter train travel +34 % February-March 2026 amid a fuel crisis (Newcastle Herald, 16 April 2026, via an aggregator) - the 2024-25 targets predate it.

HW), :526-560 balance_destinations under B.activity.destination_balancing = doubly_constrained (definition); B.external.commute_share_to_core = 0.1377 (measured, 2011 census JTW) RE-READ AT 079a49a3: 3 registry key(s) named here resolve with the same value and status; every file:line named exists; no model change touched it since 1b14e559 (registry diff: launcher-only RUN.sample.arm_fraction_floor, RUN.machine.free_ram_margin_gib, other_process_max_cores, probe_max_host_cpu_pct; Java diff: timing logs, probes, a lookup index).noneWorkplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2112.120712026-09-08

Floetteroed's statement of the position is the clearest available: the assignment relies on approximate minimisation of an EQUILIBRIUM GAP measuring, for every agent, how much that agent could improve its score by changing its plan if all other agents kept theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium', and the method 'aims to reduce the gap in subsequent MATSim iterations, steering the simulation process towards a state that has a low gap, and hence may be deemed to be near an equilibrium point'. He names the reproducible computation of point equilibria as 'the single most important advantage' of the traditional four-step / static-assignment model - an advantage MATSim does not have by default - and supplies the emulation and greedo contribs that add gap minimisation to the loop, illustrated on a multimodal Greater Stockholm scenario with all-day route, departure-time and mode choice. The wider theory agrees: MATSim targets a STOCHASTIC user equilibrium (minimum PERCEIVED cost) rather than a Nash equilibrium; best-response dynamics carry no convergence guarantee, though if they converge they converge to an equilibrium. No published convergence rate exists for a multimodal MATSim scenario: relaxation is asserted by observation, not proved.https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/baug/ivt/ivt-dam/events/2023/09/05/abstracts/Floetteroed_MUM_2023.pdf2026-11-06

The MATSim planParamCalibration extension does exactly that - a designated subpopulation carries its surveyed plan under the KeepLastSelected strategy so those plans are the ground truth, the remaining agents generate alternatives by the ordinary strategies, and CMA-ES maximises a logit-like log-likelihood over the planCalcScore parameters (mode constants, marginal utility of travelling, of distance and of money, daily monetary constants, typical and minimal activity durations, line-switch, waiting, late-arrival and early-departure terms) at each MATSim iteration, writing the result back into the config for the next one. It stops on a designated iteration or on convergence, the default being an average estimated difference below 0.001. Tested on a 2023 street-interview trip-diary survey plus mobile-location commuting arrays at 100 m grid accuracy, the maximum log-likelihood is stable over twenty MATSim iterations and essentially unchanged whether the calibration population is respondents alone or respondents plus 100k, 300k, 600k or one million commuting records - the claimed proof that the estimator is auto-adaptive to population scale. The price of the architecture is exactly the data an aggregate-only city lacks: the likelihood's observations are unit-record plans.https://www.matsim.org/conferences/mum2024/presentations/MUM2024_Lu.pdf2026-09-08

The cross-entropy method is a Monte-Carlo importance-sampling search and is the most expensive family: one published SUMO calibration of a three-intersection model spent 98,304 simulation evaluations. Bayesian optimisation over a surrogate is the current answer for a small budget (see the surrogate row). I9IIdentifiability under many simultaneous targetsPARTIALCAL.objective.independent_targets = 10 (derived) 'the loop refuses to move more free parameters than this'; src/calibrate/calibrate.py:31-37 'It refuses to fit more parameters than the data identifies', :699 n_free_allowed; src/calibrate/fit.py:22-25 '13 of the 67 identify nothing in MATSim... roughly four mode-share degrees of freedom'; fit.py:499-502 lr_scheduled_runtime marked unscorable 'a schedule INPUT'; grep 'eligib' in src/calibrate: 0 hits RE-READ AT 079a49a3: 1 registry key(s) named here resolve with the same value and status; every file:line named exists; no model change touched it since 1b14e559 (registry diff: launcher-only RUN.sample.arm_fraction_floor, RUN.machine.free_ram_margin_gib, other_process_max_cores, probe_max_host_cpu_pct; Java diff: timing logs, probes, a lookup index).noneA parameter set is identified only if distinct parameter values produce distinguishable outputs on the targets you actually hold, and the simulation-calibration literature is explicit that when a model is over-parametrised relative to its targets, 'non-identifiability can arise, making it theoretically impossible to locate the true parameter value'. The published remedy is not a better optimiser but a different answer: report an ELIGIBILITY SET - the set of all parameter values whose simulated outputs match the data - constructed to carry rigorous frequentist guarantees, extended to multivariate outputs by a feature-extraction-then-aggregation construction. The counting rule underneath is what binds a mode-share calibration: K shares that sum to one contain K-1 independent numbers, so scoring twelve modelled modes against a five-mode survey does not supply twelve independent targets. The only way to buy identifiability for more parameters is to add targets of a DIFFERENT kind - link counts, boardings, trip-length and duration distributions - not more shares of the same total. In dynamic OD calibration, 'the first formulation estimates the whole set of time-dependent OD matrices SIMULTANEOUSLY for the entire time period in one calibration round. The second formulation estimates and calibrates OD matrices SEQUENTIALLY one at a time for each time frame. Most optimization-based studies have used the simultaneous approach, since the available sequential methods may lose accuracy due to giving up some information in the transition between time frames' - while the simultaneous form 'is incapable of handling a stream of data for real-time or online demand calibration'. The same paper states the bind that makes the choice matter at all: 'this optimization problem is underdetermined for large-scale networks since the number of roads with traffic measurement is usually several orders of magnitude smaller than the number of all roads in the network', and it names the standard architecture as BI-LEVEL - an upper-level discrepancy minimisation over an inner assignment that must be re-solved at every candidate, where 'performing several DTAs for each optimization task demand considerable computational resources'. The selection protocol before the cutoff 'resembles a MNL choice model', P(i|C) = exp(mu S_i)/sum exp(mu S_j) with mu = brainExpBeta, and the chapter notes that BestPlanSelector is the same selector with an infinite mu. So the pre-cutoff share is a logit-dispersed mixture over each agent's remembered plans and the post-cutoff share is the same population collapsed toward its arg-max: switching innovation off changes the estimator, not only the amount of search. Assignment theory says the same thing from the other side - a low dispersion parameter concentrates flow on the perceived-best alternative and the pattern approaches deterministic user equilibrium, which is the classic 'unrealistic route concentration' that stochastic user equilibrium was introduced to cure. The document and process layer

layering

verdict
The seven layers of docs/HANDOVER_CONTRACT.md:24-32 exist and are where the contract says; the split simulator docs/ vs cities/<city>/docs/ (§9.171) holds - docs/README.md lists every docs/ child except the empty docs/reference/ directory. The layering breaks in three places: (1) the generated scoreboard and runs blocks on the board read a RUNNING arm and are committed, so a fact that expires lives on the board as settled prose - against HANDOVER_CONTRACT.md:80-83 ('/handoff never states one as settled: it goes in §0'); at HEAD the board read 20261008T212704_250it_25pct at iteration 26 'status running' for four weeks after the operator stopped it at 50 on 9 October (in-flight fix on this branch). (2) Rules have four homes: the run rules sit in .claude/CLAUDE.md (Runs), the board's 'Do not re-raise' (STATUS.md:128-135), the brief §3 (NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:51-59) and runs-and-economics.md 'Rules that stand' (:40-46). (3) The record's numbering is not in file order and §9.85-§9.223 sit under the '## 15.' heading in markdown structure (DECISIONS.md:8111 then 9.85 at :8327), which the header (DECISIONS.md:8-14, 42-49) documents rather than fixes.

detail
Digest + GOAL 138 + board 142 + brief 59 + one position page (76-104) = 415-443 lines, inside 'about 600' (HANDOVER_CONTRACT.md:20). Each layer is inside its own row: GOAL ~140 (138), board <=170 hand lines/24,000 hand bytes (142 lines, hand bytes inside the cap per check_doc_shape), brief <=180 (59), positions <=130/14,000 (all ok; sampling-and-families 15,396 bytes on disk but 7,342 counted - the generated families table is excluded), city README <=160 (exactly 160), record 16,000+ (18,568).
what_the_line_count_hides
The budget is stated in lines and the cost is bytes. The four onboarding documents are 8.2 + 22.9 + 14.9 + ~13 KB = ~59 KB, plus .claude/CLAUDE.md 19.7 KB auto-loaded and the onboard skill 8.6 KB - about 87 KB (~22k tokens) before Phase 1. The brief is 59 lines but 14,884 bytes (252 chars a line; 8 lines over 600 chars) because the generated lane block (~6 KB, 8 tasks) is rendered twice - into the board's Next (STATUS.md:97-108) and the brief §1 (NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:22-33) - so every /onboard reads it twice. The city README is at exactly its 160-line cap.
recommendation

Recommendations, ranked

Ranked by what each would prevent or move × how cheap it is. A repeat tag marks one an earlier report already issued; the process audit counts them against this report too.

  1. Copy every plans checkpoint out of results/raw and pin resumable or died runs against trim, reclaim and prune code
    The host reset destroyed the treatment's it.25 and it.50 checkpoints and all 81 aborted raw directories; nothing in results_store.py reads resumable or died, and prune_run.py deletes ITERS on a false premise.
    change: results_store.py trim/reclaim and prune_run.py honour resumable/died; run_matsim.py copies the newest N.plans.xml.gz (~1.0-1.2 GB) plus the records into a declared RUN.storage checkpoint dir at each dump, pause and death; resolve_warm_start falls back to it · guard: a unit test that a trimmed resumable run still resolves a warm start
  2. Make --pause stop after the next completed plans dump, and skip a checkpoint that fails a gzip check code
    A pause mid-iteration repeats up to 24 iterations (~3.4 h at 508 s) and a kill in the dump leaves a truncated checkpoint resolve_warm_start picks anyway (run_matsim.py:2449, 264-278).
    change: run_matsim.py stop_run waits for the iteration's plans write; resolve_warm_start runs gzip -t before choosing · guard: test_launch_hardening.py case for a truncated checkpoint
  3. Relaunch F39's treatment from iteration 0 on a fresh stated-cost approval, alone on the host model repeat ×3
    The pair is the only open measurement of the pt frequency term (#175 #98 #94); D29 has 24.2 h of 40 left against the control's 27.9 h wall, and the next arm should be the first one with checkpoints that survive the host.
    change: run.py --run-config f39_headway_25pct after recommendation 1 lands; Windows Update paused (D19), Blender closed, a 40 h ceiling · guard: arm_cost.py price line; compare_runs.py --modes against 20260929T072135_250it_25pct
    predicts: bus, light_rail up; heavy_rail, ferry down — toward their targets; size: unmeasured at the horizon; the stopped arm read -34.2 / -68.2 / +115.7 / +75.1 % at it.50 against -30.7 / -74.0 / +119.3 / +95.4 % on the control at it.250, not comparable iterations
